statement: Khadijah was the first person to believe.
notes: Agreed among the historians; Bukhari 3 shows her immediate support.

statement: Ali, Zayd ibn Harithah and Abu Bakr were the next believers; the order among them is disputed; a common formulation names Abu Bakr first of men, Ali first of boys, Zayd first of freed slaves.
alternatives: Reports differ on whether Ali or Abu Bakr was first after Khadijah.

statement: The Prophet said: Allah sent me to you and you said 'you lie', while Abu Bakr said 'he has spoken the truth' and supported me with himself and his wealth; will you not leave my companion alone.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked against Bukhari 3661. The occasion was a quarrel between Abu Bakr and Umar; the script says 'some of his Companions had a disagreement'.

statement: Abu Bakr was a well-liked merchant; through him Uthman, az-Zubayr, Abd ar-Rahman ibn Awf, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and Talhah accepted Islam.
Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas: for seven days I was a third of Islam.
Ammar: I saw the Messenger of Allah with none but five slaves, two women and Abu Bakr.
Amr ibn Abasah asked who was with him: 'a free man and a slave'; he was told he could not follow him openly then and to return when he heard he had prevailed.
notes: Direct speech. Content found in the Muslim dataset; wording of the latter part to be checked against the Arabic. The narration identifies the two as Abu Bakr and Bilal.

statement: Abu Dharr sent his brother to Makkah, was not satisfied, came himself, did not ask about the Prophet, and was hosted by Ali without either asking the other.
notes: Machine-checked for the first half of the narration.

statement: On the third night Ali asked, Abu Dharr told him after taking his promise, Ali confirmed and led him; he accepted Islam, was told to return to his people, proclaimed his faith in the mosque, was beaten, and al-Abbas shielded him citing Ghifar's position on the Syrian trade route.
notes: Second half of the narration written from memory; the dataset text was truncated at lookup. Reviewer to check each detail and the quoted words of Ali.

statement: Early believers included some of the nobility but more of the young, poor, clanless and enslaved.
Heraclius asked Abu Sufyan whether the nobles or the weak followed him ('the weak'; 'such are the followers of the messengers') and whether any left the religion out of displeasure ('no').
notes: Direct speech; the meeting took place years later, after Hudaybiyyah.
